claims.text: The nanoparticles begin as spherical, solid, random equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu particles with an FCC lattice parameter of 3.52 Å.
Melting onset and progression in ultrasmall FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by enhanced element-specific diffusion rather than formation of a stable surface-liquid shell.
Fe and Cu are preferentially mobilized before the other constituent elements.
Preferential Fe and Cu mobilization arises from local energetic instabilities and differences in elemental melting points.
Fe atoms have local potential energies approximately 0.5 eV higher than the relevant comparison atoms in the multielement FCC lattice.
Cu has an inherently lower elemental melting point that contributes to its early mobility.
Preferential early mobility occurs primarily within two to three surface layers at approximately 900 K.
Enhanced diffusion initiated by Fe and Cu propagates from the nanoparticle surface into the core.
Element-specific diffusion gradually disrupts the solid phase.
The melting pathway bypasses a discrete, persistent surface-premelting liquid-shell phase.
The nanoparticle melting temperature increases with radius and approaches the bulk limit according to an approximately inverse-radius two-phase melting relation.
The fitted bulk melting-temperature limit is 2184 K.
Fe and Cu become mobile at lower temperatures in the nanoparticles than in the bulk material.
The overall elemental distribution remains largely unclustered during premelting and melting.
The proposed behavior applies to particles with radii of approximately 5–40 Å under the specified simulation protocol.
The proposed behavior becomes more pronounced above radii of approximately 7.5–10 Å.
Initial size-dependent deviations and minor short-range clustering trends become negligible above radii of approximately 7.5–10 Å.
The quantitative radius dependence and mobility-onset temperatures may depend on the interatomic potential, simulation timescale, and heating protocol.
Element-resolved mean-square displacement can distinguish preferential early Fe and Cu mobility from nondiscriminatory atomic mobility.
Common-neighbor analysis, polyhedral-template matching, and atomic visualization can test whether a persistent surface-liquid shell forms.

contradictions.description: The protocol is described as NVE while also using velocity rescaling during heating and equilibration. Repeated velocity rescaling changes the system energy and is not a strictly microcanonical NVE trajectory unless it is confined to initialization or separately defined preparation stages.
